chapter_title: Concerning why Some shall delay to come forth from
spiritual_reading:
This passage is too fragmentary to yield a coherent continuous spiritual sequence. The subject, the actions, and the objects that would govern the direction of influx and the quality of the state are missing at the ellipses, so several different spiritual senses could fit without warrant.

Best reconstruction from what remains, with uncertainty noted:

A secondary governing principle within the human mind enters a state of collapse, and in that collapse the unified operation that should have held the lower things in order becomes divided. A first capacity remains for a time in a limited state of awareness, and a further capacity is present but not yet able to act openly. A brief state is measured out in which other assisting powers are permitted to stand by in readiness, holding their position so that the order that remains is not broken. They restrain their action and wait through a period of delay until the bound state is released and the obstruction is removed. Even then, they do not at once advance into full operation, but continue in restraint, approaching only so far as the restored freedom allows.

Uncertainties: what “fall” is from (truth into falsity, or good into temptation), what “one” signifies here (unity, first principle, or a remnant), what the “hour” qualifies (a fixed state, a short temptation, or a measured permission), who the “others” are (truths, affections, or operative faculties), and what kind of “freeing” is meant (release from falsity, from compulsion, or from bondage to evil).

fills.notes: The surviving clause begins “The second … if he shall fall …”. In the oldest cosmological register, what “comes” to a secondary power is not a person speaking but a law or ordering influx. This also prepares the later verbs of restraint and delay as regulated permissions within order.

The fall is best taken as a collapse from an appointed degree or station (a correspondential ‘place’), not yet specifying moral cause. This matches the spiritual translation’s ‘state of collapse’ and keeps the substrate impersonal.

The text immediately moves into measured delay and coordinated action by ‘others’. A procedural verb (“they set”, i.e., establish a measure) fits the cosmic-mechanical tone and introduces the next “one … one hour …” as a fixed permission.

The repeated “one … one hour …” calls for a unit-of-state framing. In correspondences, “measure” is the determination of a state by order; it avoids later devotional language and makes “hour” a qualified state-duration.

“Others who shall … and they remain.” The ‘others’ are assisting powers held in readiness; “stand apart” expresses separation without rupture—present but restrained, matching the translation’s ‘stand by in readiness, holding their position’.

“They shall delay until they … he is freed,” requires an intervening condition that authorizes their restraint. In the substrate, delay is governed by permission under order; ‘permission until’ bridges the waiting and the release without importing institutional terms.

“they delay to come toward …” points to a limit of approach. In correspondences a ‘boundary’ is the fixed margin of a state into which higher powers may not yet enter. This matches ‘approaching only so far as the restored freedom allows’.

assessment: The chapter is extremely lacunose, so restorations can only be made at the level of correspondential function: fall as loss of station, ‘hour’ as a measured state, ‘others’ as restrained assisting powers, and approach as limited by a boundary. Exact idiom is uncertain; the fills aim to keep the impersonal, law-like tone of the oldest cosmological layer.
